traditions.name: Demonological reading of UFOs
traditions.earliest_attestation: 1969–1975 CE (Vallée, Keel, Seraphim Rose); continued in Christian ufology
traditions.scholarly_note: An interpretive tradition, not an organized religion: writers who read UFO encounters as the same phenomenon earlier ages called demons, fairies or fallen angels. Jacques Vallée and John Keel framed it as folklore continuity; Orthodox and evangelical writers framed it as demonic deception.

deities.earliest_attestation: 1969 CE (Vallée, Passport to Magonia, folklore-continuity form); demonic reading 1970–1975 (Keel; Seraphim Rose)
primary_sources: Seraphim Rose, Orthodoxy and the Religion of the Future (1975)
deities.summary: The beings people meet as aliens are not visitors from other planets. They are the same intelligences that every earlier age met under its own names — demons, the fair folk, the jinn, the fallen angels — wearing the costume of the space age. They take whatever form a culture expects; Christian writers such as Seraphim Rose add that they deceive and lead people away from God with promises of hidden knowledge and a new humanity.

facets.facet_name: Fallen angels in the guise of space visitors
facets.core_claim: The 'aliens' are demons. Their messages of cosmic brotherhood, their abductions and their hybrid programmes are the old rebellion against God in a new form, as the Watchers once came down and mingled with humanity.
facets.scholarly_note: Christian-apologetic form: Seraphim Rose (1975), Gary Bates (2004).

facets.facet_name: One phenomenon behind fairies, demons and aliens
facets.core_claim: The same intelligence appears in every century in the shape its witnesses expect: fairies and incubi in the medieval countryside, airships in the 1890s, flying saucers after 1947. The form changes; the behaviour does not.
facets.scholarly_note: Folklore-continuity form: Jacques Vallée, Passport to Magonia (1969); John Keel, Operation Trojan Horse (1970), who called them 'ultraterrestrials'.

basis: This reading identifies the grey visitors of abduction accounts as demons
Both are non-human intelligences that appear, take people and deliver messages
parallels.syncretic_source: Seraphim Rose, Orthodoxy and the Religion of the Future (1975); Gary Bates, Alien Intrusion (2004)

basis: Christian ufology reads the Watchers of 1 Enoch, who came down and mingled with humanity, as the same beings people now call aliens
Both descend from the sky, cross the boundary between heaven and earth, and corrupt humanity
parallels.syncretic_source: Christian ufology since the 1970s (e.g. Gary Bates, Alien Intrusion, 2004)

basis: Both are unseen intelligent beings that share the world with humans and can take visible forms
Both are blamed for abductions, possession and deceptive visions
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Some Muslim writers identify UFO beings with jinn; this is a popular reading, not a teaching of Islamic law or theology.

basis: Sky-beings produce hybrid offspring with humans
In 1 Enoch the hybrids are the Nephilim; in abduction lore they are the alien-human hybrids
parallels.scholarly_caveat: The parallel is drawn by modern ufologists and Christian writers; 1 Enoch says nothing of spacecraft.

basis: Crowley's 1919 drawing of Lam, with its huge bald head and small features, is read as an early image of a grey
Typhonian writers present Lam as an entity contacted from 'outside', as contactees describe the greys
parallels.syncretic_source: Kenneth Grant's Typhonian writings (from 1972) and later ufology
parallels.scholarly_caveat: The grey-alien image took shape in the 1960s–80s; the link to Crowley's drawing is a later reading.

basis: Both are sky-beings who come down and teach humanity arts and knowledge
Ancient-astronaut writers read both as visitors from another world
parallels.syncretic_source: Erich von Däniken, Chariots of the Gods? (1968); Zecharia Sitchin, The 12th Planet (1976)

basis: Channelers place Ashtar's fleet within the Galactic Federation of Light
Both are star-nations said to watch over Earth's coming transition
Contactees receive Ashtar as a benevolent space commander
Christian ufology reads the same messages as demonic deception
parallels.syncretic_source: Contactee movement (George Van Tassel, 1952) vs. Christian ufology (Seraphim Rose, 1975)
